title: setAsideBufferSize persists after a client is deauthorized and silently resurrects on re-auth
story: story-042 — per-client setAsideBuffer added to skimSurplus
description: setSetAsideBuffer (AYieldStrategy.sol#L253-L259) writes setAsideBufferSize[client] = bufferPercent unconditionally — no _authorizedClients.contains(client) check. Symmetrically, setClient(client, false) (L183-L193) removes the address from _authorizedClients but does not zero setAsideBufferSize[client]. The child's _accrueSurplusShares (ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol#L487) reads setAsideBufferSize[client] from parent storage during the next skim. If the owner re-authorizes the same address via setClient(client, true), the stale buffer percentage takes effect on the next skim — no re-write required — silently diverting surplus.
impact: No direct loss. Misallocated yield on the post-reauth skim: surplus that should have flowed to the recipient is diverted to the re-authorized client per the stale buffer percent. Magnitude bounded by the size of the next skim and the stale buffer setting. Operator footgun within C-01 envelope; no external attacker leverage because every client is protocol-owned (per AYieldStrategy.sol#L246 AUDITOR NOTE).
attackPath: 2. Owner calls setClient(clientA, false). Storage: _authorizedClients removes clientA; setAsideBufferSize[clientA] still equals 50 (never zeroed).
3. Time passes. Owner re-adds clientA via setClient(clientA, true) — perhaps after an address rotation or post-incident re-enable.
4. Next skim: _accrueSurplusShares reads setAsideBufferSize[clientA] = 50 and diverts 50% of clientA's principal-weighted surplus to clientA — even though no fresh setSetAsideBuffer call was made.
assumptions: Operator may toggle client authorization (a designed operational pattern).
Operator does not re-verify all per-client buffer settings after re-auth (a realistic omission).
externalRequirements: setClient(client, false) followed by setClient(client, true) with no intervening setSetAsideBuffer(client, 0).
recommendation: Either (a) in setClient(client, false), explicitly zero setAsideBufferSize[client] and emit SetAsideBufferSet(client, oldPercent, 0); or (b) require _authorizedClients.contains(client) in setSetAsideBuffer (rejecting both stale writes and writes to never-authorized addresses); or (c) document the resurrection-on-reauth semantics in the NatSpec. Option (a) gives the cleanest invariant: setAsideBufferSize[client] != 0 ⇒ _authorizedClients.contains(client). Aligns with feedback_revert_over_silent_clamp.md.
